subject: Threshold value selection in session code.

messages.author: cbebdaa89cf1945e
messages.subject: Threshold value selection in session code.
parts:
Hi Wallace Team! I hope this email finds you well.

I'm currently running a full niche modeling analysis through Wallace's shiny. When I get to the Visualize module, I choose to make a prediction map using the 10 percentile training presence as a thresholding rule, and I finish the workflow by downloading the documented code.

My goal is to share the code so that other people can review and reproduce it. When I reviewed the "Visualization" section of the code to get the binary prediction map, I found the following statement "Generate a map of the Maxent generated model with a p10 threshold rule of 0.385493114590645". Where does this threshold value come from?  I have reviewed the code in previous steps, and it doesn't document exactly how Wallace obtained this value. Therefore, if there is no line in the code that tells me how to obtain this threshold value, then the code that I'm generating isn't completely reproducible.

If I'm using the 10 percentile training presence as a thresholding rule, What command or line of code can I add to get the exact threshold value to generate the binary map prediction?

Thanks for your time and help.

Best, Jhan

messages.author: 881c0dd9c7b0d196
messages.subject: Re: Threshold value selection in session code.
parts:
Hi Jhan,
Thanks for bringing this to our attention. One of our team members is now fixing the session code to make it more intuitive.

In the meantime, I have some suggestions for a workaround. One is to use Wallace v1.1, in which the session code explicitly gives steps to determining the threshold value. The other option is to continue using v1.9, but you can add the following lines of code to the session code to determine the value of the threshold and how to change it if you want to.

Add the following to the chunk below where it says "### Visualize Generate a map of the maxnet generated model with with a “p10” threshold
rule of ...... " You will need to change the 'XX' to the letters used for your species.

## change Maxent to Maxnet
predSel_XX <- predictMaxnet(m_XX, bgMask_XX,
                                   type = "cloglog",
                                   clamp = TRUE)
occPredVals <- raster::extract(predSel_XX, occs_XX[ , c("longitude", "latitude")])

#select a threshold
tenpct <-quantile(occPredVals, probs = 0.1) #10pct
mtp <- quantile(occPredVals, probs = 0.0) #mtp

# Applied selected threshold
predSel_thr <- predSel_Hc > tenpct
plot(predSel_thr)

I hope that helps, and again, thank you for bringing this to our attention.
-Bethany, The Wallace team
